children: , the advanced-lithography equipment leader, faces a fresh capacity challenge as management explores pushing EUV production beyond 110 systems in 2028, according to JPMorgan analysts cited by Reuters. The U.S. shares gained approximately 1.6% to $1,626.48 Thursday, based on the latest price shown, versus $1,630.48 earlier in the session. The valuation picture is already demanding: the shares trade 28.86% above the roughly $1,260 GF Value estimate, suggesting investors are pricing in a sizable chunk of ASML's future growth.

The bottleneck is increasingly inside ASML's own factories. Reuters reported that the company is nearly sold out for 2027, when production capacity reaches at least 80 EUV machines. Getting to 110 systems in 2028 would mean lifting annual output by at least 37.5% from that level. JPMorgan said supplier capacity is not the main constraint; the bigger question is how quickly ASML can assemble these enormously complex machines without compromising execution.

That matters because the financial engine is already running hot. ASML generated 8.9 billion in second-quarter sales, delivered a 54% gross margin and earned 2.9 billion in net income. High-NA adoption is expected to start contributing in 2028 and build from there, giving the company another powerful growth lever. But with the stock already sitting well above GF Value, investors are paying for strong execution today: faster assembly, timely installations and sustained margins will need to keep pace with the semiconductor industry's appetite for ever-more-advanced lithography.

title: ASML Gains 1.5% as 110 EUV Machines Test Assembly Speed
